title: Full-stack web app, deployed
summary: A complete web application (frontend, your API and a database) deployed to the internet for real users, with CI/CD and monitoring.
why: This is the closest thing to an internship project you can do on your own: build, ship and keep something running for real people. It proves you can work across the stack and handle the messy parts: deployments, configuration and bugs found by real use.
brief:
Build a frontend for the API from the previous project (or a new one) and ship the whole thing so real people use it. Find two to five real users first, such as your club, classmates or a family business, and build what they need. Their feedback is part of the project.

Constraints: a TypeScript frontend with routing, forms whose client-side validation mirrors the server's rules, loading, empty and error states for every request, and a responsive layout. Deploy the frontend, API and database to free or low-cost hosting with HTTPS, separate development and production configuration, and every secret in environment variables. Set up CI/CD: lint and tests on every pull request, and an automatic deploy when main changes. Add basic monitoring: error tracking or at least structured logs, plus an uptime check.

Work like a team even if you are alone: an issue for each feature and bug, a branch and pull request for each change, and a short changelog. Keep notes on what broke in production and how you fixed it; those notes become your best interview stories.

milestones.title: Users and scope
tasks: Talk to two to five real users and write down their biggest problems
Write a one-page spec with must-haves and nice-to-haves
Open an issue for each must-have
milestones.doneWhen: The repository has a spec and an issue for every must-have, each traceable to something a user said.

milestones.title: Frontend foundation
tasks: Set up TypeScript, routing and a single API client module
Build login plus the main list and detail pages
Handle loading, empty and error states on every page
milestones.doneWhen: Every page works against the local API, and stopping the API shows a friendly error instead of a blank screen.

milestones.title: Core features
tasks: Build the create and edit flows with form validation
Build the one feature your users asked for most
Write component tests and at least one end-to-end test of the main flow
milestones.doneWhen: A new user can sign up and finish the main task, and an end-to-end test does the same in CI.

milestones.title: Deploy with CI/CD
tasks: Deploy the database, API and frontend with HTTPS
Configure environment variables separately for development and production
Make CI run lint and tests on pull requests and deploy main automatically
milestones.doneWhen: Merging a pull request into main deploys to production with no manual steps, and the live URL works.

milestones.title: Real use and monitoring
tasks: Onboard your users and collect feedback for two weeks
Add error tracking or structured logging, and an uptime check
Fix the top three issues users report
milestones.doneWhen: At least three people other than you have used the live app, and closed issues show fixes that came from their feedback.

milestones.title: Write it up
tasks: A README with the live link, screenshots, an architecture diagram and setup steps
A short post-mortem of one production bug
milestones.doneWhen: The README has a working live link, an architecture diagram and a written account of one real production issue.

stretch: An accessibility audit and fixes (keyboard use, screen reader labels, contrast)
A performance budget: measure load time and improve it
Background jobs such as email reminders
rubric: A reviewer should be able to open a live HTTPS link and complete the main flow
A reviewer should see CI that tests pull requests and deploys automatically from main
A reviewer should see loading, empty and error states handled in the interface
A reviewer should see no secrets in the repository and separate development and production configuration
A reviewer should see issues and pull requests that show how the project evolved
A reviewer should see evidence of real users, such as feedback issues or usage numbers
A reviewer should see a README with an architecture diagram and a production bug write-up
showcase: Put the live link and a 30-second demo video or GIF at the top of the README
Include an architecture diagram: frontend, API, database, hosting and the CI/CD path
Add a 'Lessons from production' section with one real bug: symptom, cause, fix and prevention
List it first on your resume, in LinkedIn's Featured section and on your portfolio
resumeBullet: Built and deployed a full-stack study planner (React, TypeScript, FastAPI, PostgreSQL) used weekly by 40 students; set up CI/CD that tests and deploys every merge, and used error monitoring to find and fix 12 user-reported bugs.
interviewTalkingPoints: A production bug: how you noticed it, found the cause and stopped it recurring
Why validation lives on both the client and the server
How your CI/CD pipeline works and what it protects against
A feature you cut or changed after user feedback, and why
What would break first if usage grew 100 times
